title: Model attestation catalog, immutable pinning, and canary gating for onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Automate end-to-end model onboarding such that every published model artifact is accompanied by an auditable attestation, an immutable version manifest used for pinning in serving configs, and an automated canary gating flow that rejects profile regressions before promotion to production. This ticket implements the CI/CD pieces: build orchestration, attestation generation (KMS-backed), metadata cataloging, pin manifest generation, and canary traffic gating with automated rollback on quality/latency regressions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) CI build produces model artifact (tar.gz) + performance profile JSON + signed attestation stored in model-registry; 2) Attestation contains build hash, kernel/profile fingerprint, container image digest, build pipeline run id, and KMS signature reference; 3) A manifest file (manifest.json) is generated that pins the exact artifact digest and runtime compatibility matrix; 4) On merge, pipeline publishes to staging with a canary rollout job that runs automated evals and latency probes; 5) Canary gating rejects publish if token-cost or P95 latency regress by >5% or if eval accuracy drops >2% relative to baseline; 6) Promotion job only runs with approved attestation and passing canary checks; 7) All artifacts and provenance are queryable in the Console model catalog and audit logs show build->attest->promote steps.
implementation_notes: High-level flow: 1) Build step (gha/gke-runner) exports artifact, profile, and SBOM-like metadata. 2) Attestation service calls KMS to create a detached attestation; store attestation in model-registry S3 bucket with encryption. 3) Publish manifest.json with pinned digest and compatibility tags to catalog DB and artifact registry. 4) Deploy a temporary canary in staging via deployment pipeline that routes 2% traffic for 60 minutes; run eval suite (promptset + unit tests) and latency microbenchmarks. 5) Canary job emits metrics to canary-dashboard and posts status to pipeline. 6) Promotion job requires: attestation present, canary status == pass, and 1 approver from Platform Eng. Implementation details: reuse existing artifact signing library but swap from internal RSA key to KMS-backed asymmetric signing using 'attest-v2' API. Store provenance links in model-catalog table with TTL for ephemeral fields. Edge cases: large models (>20GB) use incremental chunked upload; ensure manifest supports chunk index.
timeline: Week 1: Build & attestation prototype + unit tests; Week 2: Catalog integration, manifest schema, and KMS rotation story; Week 3: Canary job and gating thresholds wired to pipeline; Week 4: Security review, docs, and rollout to beta customers.
notes_and_tradeoffs:
- Attestation vs full image signing: attestation keeps artifact storage cheap and avoids mandating container builds for all models.
- KMS-backed signing introduces dependency on cloud KMS; mitigated by HSM-backed key with cross-region replication.
- Strict pinning improves reproducibility but makes emergency patching harder; we will support 'pinned alias' that maps to promoted artifacts with audit trail.
- Canary thresholds are conservative initially (5% latency or 2% quality) and will be tuned after 2 weeks of data.
review_feedback:
- Security asked for key rotation plan and retention policy for attestations (added to implementation_notes).
- Platform PM requested a UI mock for manifest inspection in Console (see Confluence link).
- SRE suggested adding a fallback policy that automatically falls back to previous pinned model if canary control errors exceed 1%.
next_steps: 1) Finalize manifest schema and JSON-LD fields; 2) Implement attestation upload + KMS signing in rw-model-ci; 3) Add canary eval harness to pipeline using existing eval-runner; 4) Run beta with internal teams; 5) Open security review ticket and schedule architecture review.
